title: U.S. House · Illinois's 17th District
area: Northwestern Illinois, including Rockford, the Quad Cities (Moline/Rock Island), and Peoria-area suburbs.

context.text: Incumbent Eric Sorensen ran unopposed in the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary. Dillan Vancil defeated Julie Bickelhaupt in the Republican primary, 58.4% to 41.6%.

candidates.name: Eric Sorensen
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed

summary.text: Eric Sorensen is the Democratic U.S. Representative for Illinois's 17th District, first elected in 2022 and seeking a third term. He worked for more than two decades as a television meteorologist in Illinois before entering politics, and sits on the House Agriculture and Armed Services committees.

background.text: Born and raised in Rockford, Illinois, according to his official House biography.

Earned a bachelor's degree from Northern Illinois University (Ballotpedia lists the graduation year inconsistently, so it is omitted here); Wikipedia reports he studied communications and meteorology there and graduated from Boylan Catholic High School.
Began his career as a television meteorologist at KTRE in Lufkin, Texas (1999–2000) and later worked in Tyler, Texas, before serving as chief meteorologist at WREX in Rockford from 2003 to 2014.

Became senior meteorologist at WQAD in the Quad Cities in 2014 and retired from television in 2021; his House biography describes more than two decades as a local TV meteorologist in Central and Northwestern Illinois.
Worked in communications for UnityPoint Health after leaving television and served on the boards of Clock, Inc. and the Project of the Quad Cities.
Announced his candidacy for Congress on November 10, 2021, after Rep. Cheri Bustos said she would not seek re-election, and defeated Republican Esther Joy King in the November 2022 general election.
Took office in January 2023. Re-elected in 2024, defeating Republican Joseph McGraw with 54.4% of the vote, and renominated without opposition in the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary.

In the 119th Congress serves on the House Agriculture Committee and the Armed Services Committee (Readiness, and Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittees); in the 118th Congress he served on Agriculture and on Science, Space, and Technology, where he was ranking member of the Space and Aeronautics subcommittee.
Resides in Moline with his partner, Shawn, according to his official House biography.

priorities.text: My top priority is addressing rising costs that are hurting Illinoisans from the grocery store to the gas pump. I'm also committed to bringing down out-of-control drug prices, especially for our seniors.
I believe everyone has the right to be healthy, which is why I'm working in Congress to make health care more affordable, accessible, and efficient.

We need to find ways to protect our homes and farms from draughts, floods, and other adverse weather events while investing in clean power sources that will create sustainable, good-paying jobs right here in our district.

positions.summary: Says reproductive health care decisions should be made between a patient and their doctor, not lawmakers, and that he will work to remove barriers to reproductive care.
positions.quote: I believe that reproductive health care decisions should be made between an individual and their doctor – not lawmakers. ... I will continue to work in Congress to break down barriers to accessing reproductive care, not building them.

positions.summary: Says the climate is changing and calls for investing in clean power sources while protecting communities from severe-weather damage.
positions.quote: We need to find ways to protect our homes and farms from draughts, floods, and other adverse weather events while investing in clean power sources that will create sustainable, good-paying jobs right here in our district.

positions.summary: Says he is working to invest more into local law enforcement agencies to support training, recruitment, and retention.
positions.quote: As your Representative, I am taking strides to invest more into local law enforcement agencies to support their training needs, help them better retain and recruit officers, and build better relationships with the communities they serve.

positions.summary: Says he wants to protect and expand the Affordable Care Act to cover preexisting conditions and let Medicare negotiate prescription drug prices.
positions.quote: I believe we need to protect and expand the Affordable Care Act (ACA) to ensure preexisting conditions are covered. I also support solutions that bring down the cost of prescription drugs, like allowing Medicare to negotiate with pharmaceutical companies.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the Committee on Agriculture (General Farm Commodities, Risk Management and Credit; Conservation, Research and Biotechnology) and the House Committee on Armed Services (Readiness; Tactical Air and Land Forces).

candidates.name: Dillan Vancil
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 17, 2026 Republican primary with 58.4% of the vote

summary.text: Dillan Vancil is the Republican nominee for Illinois's 17th District. He is a former railroad engineer and the founder of the Dame Fine Coffee shop chain in west-central Illinois, and has served on the West Central school board. He won the March 2026 Republican primary over Carroll County Board Chair Julie Bickelhaupt and describes his campaign as focused on small business, energy, and affordability.

background.text: Born in Illinois; graduated from West-Central High School, according to his questionnaire answers to Tri States Public Radio, which listed his age as 33 as of March 17, 2026.
Worked as a railroad engineer before becoming a business owner, according to NPR Illinois.

Founder and CEO of Dame Fine Coffee, a chain of coffee shops in west-central Illinois and eastern Iowa (NPR Illinois reported seven shops in August 2025); the name is an acronym of his family members' first names.
Served on the West Central School Board (former vice president), and lists membership on the Eagleview Community Health board and the Monmouth Chamber of Commerce board.
Lives west of Monmouth, Illinois, according to NPR Illinois.
Won the March 17, 2026 Republican primary for the 17th District with 58.4% of the vote over Julie Bickelhaupt (41.6%).
Told NPR Illinois he entered the race because he wants to make it easier to start and grow small businesses.
